notes: Replaced cloudwatch-data-protection-stored-data with cloudwatch-data-protection-retroactivity to avoid overlap with the unmasking card's explanation. Replaced codebuild-compute-type-fixed-build with codebuild-startbuild-compute-override-scope, apigw-rest-testinvokemethod-authorization with apigw-rest-testinvoke-deployment-prerequisite, and codebuild-test-report-build-status with codebuild-test-report-file-input because the replacements have more explicit support in the opened official sources. Replaced lambda-invoke-dryrun-execution with lambda-invoke-dryrun-permission-validation to test permission behavior instead of a fact suggested by the term DryRun. Replaced ssm-advanced-parameter-expiration with ssm-expiration-policy-value-update to test value-update behavior instead of a fact suggested by the term Expiration.

cards.statement: AWS KMS GenerateDataKey supports returning a plaintext data key along with its KMS-encrypted copy.
cards.explanation: Use the plaintext data key to encrypt application data, then discard it. Keep the encrypted copy so the data key can be recovered later.

cards.statement: AWS KMS treats encryption context keys and values as case-insensitive during decryption.
cards.explanation: Decrypting symmetric KMS ciphertext uses the encryption context supplied during encryption, with exact case-sensitive matches for its keys and values.
cards.misconception: Encryption context matching ignores differences in letter case.

cards.statement: AWS KMS propagates a new grant's permissions with strong consistency after CreateGrant succeeds.
cards.explanation: New KMS grants propagate with eventual consistency. A caller can pass the returned grant token to use the grant before propagation finishes.
cards.misconception: A successful CreateGrant response makes the grant immediately consistent throughout KMS.

cards.statement: Amazon S3 initializes a new bucket's object encryption configuration with SSE-S3 by default.
cards.explanation: New S3 buckets start with SSE-S3 default encryption, so uploads receive server-side encryption. Developers can configure a different supported default.
cards.volatilityNote: The initial bucket encryption default is service behavior that AWS can change.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3)

cards.statement: Amazon S3 stores the customer-provided encryption key with an object uploaded using SSE-C.
cards.explanation: For SSE-C, S3 discards the supplied key after using it. The caller retains the key and provides it again for operations that decrypt the object.
cards.misconception: S3 retains SSE-C encryption keys so the client can retrieve the object later with its usual credentials.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with customer-provided keys (SSE-C)

cards.statement: Amazon S3 checks the caller's kms:Decrypt permission when downloading an SSE-KMS object.
cards.explanation: S3 decrypts the object's encrypted data key through KMS during download. The caller needs access to that KMS key to read the object.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)

cards.statement: With policy-based access, AWS KMS checks the key policy and the caller's IAM policy for cross-account use.
cards.explanation: The key-owning account authorizes the external principal in its key policy. The caller's account delegates that permission through an IAM policy.

source.title: Allowing users in other accounts to use a KMS key

cards.statement: Rotating an AWS KMS key rewrites existing ciphertext with the key's newly generated key material.
cards.explanation: KMS rotation changes material used for new encryption rather than rewriting existing ciphertext. Decryption uses the material that originally encrypted the data.
cards.misconception: Key rotation re-encrypts data that applications encrypted with the previous key material.

cards.statement: AWS KMS supports automatic rotation for asymmetric KMS keys used for encryption.
cards.explanation: Automatic KMS rotation applies to eligible symmetric encryption keys. Rotate an asymmetric key by creating a replacement key and updating application references.
cards.misconception: Asymmetric encryption keys use the same automatic rotation feature as symmetric encryption keys.
cards.volatilityNote: AWS could extend automatic rotation eligibility to additional key types.

cards.statement: AWS Private CA uses the public key in a certificate signing request when issuing a certificate.
cards.explanation: Private CA copies the CSR's SubjectPublicKeyInfo into the certificate. That field carries the public key selected by the requester.

cards.statement: AWS Private CA IssueCertificate returns the issued certificate's PEM data in its response.
cards.explanation: IssueCertificate returns a certificate ARN. Retrieve the issued certificate with GetCertificate after issuance completes.
cards.misconception: IssueCertificate returns the certificate body synchronously instead of a reference for retrieval.

cards.statement: Amazon EC2 CreateKeyPair returns the private key material in its successful response.
cards.explanation: Save the private key returned by CreateKeyPair. EC2 retains the matching public key for instances that use the key pair.

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs applies a new data protection policy to previously ingested sensitive log events.
cards.explanation: A data protection policy applies to log events ingested after the policy takes effect. Older events retain their original masking status.
cards.misconception: Creating a data protection policy masks sensitive data in historical log events.

source.title: Help protect sensitive log data with masking

cards.statement: CloudWatch Logs GetLogEvents reveals masked values by default for a caller with logs:Unmask permission.
cards.explanation: A caller with logs:Unmask permission sets unmask=true on GetLogEvents to request the original sensitive values. Permission alone leaves the default masking in place.
cards.misconception: Granting logs:Unmask automatically makes GetLogEvents return sensitive values as plaintext.

cards.statement: Lambda function code calls KMS Decrypt to read environment values protected with client-side encryption.
cards.explanation: Client-side encrypted Lambda environment values reach the handler as ciphertext. Function code calls KMS Decrypt to recover the plaintext.

cards.statement: AWS Secrets Manager GetSecretValue can return a secret's plaintext value to an authorized caller.
cards.explanation: Secrets Manager decrypts the stored secret and returns SecretString or SecretBinary. Application code uses the returned secret value.

cards.statement: AWS Secrets Manager rotation refreshes cached values in the AWS parameters and secrets Lambda extension.
cards.explanation: The extension keeps a cached secret until its configured TTL expires. Rotating a secret does not push a new value into that cache.
cards.misconception: Rotating a secret immediately refreshes the Lambda extension's existing cache entry.
tags: AWS parameters and secrets Lambda extension

source.title: Use Secrets Manager secrets in Lambda functions

cards.statement: AWS Secrets Manager logs the returned SecretString in CloudTrail's GetSecretValue event.
cards.explanation: Secrets Manager excludes SecretString and SecretBinary values from CloudTrail records. The audit event tracks the API call rather than returning the secret's contents.
cards.misconception: CloudTrail includes the secret value returned by GetSecretValue.

cards.statement: AWS Systems Manager GetParameter returns SecureString plaintext when WithDecryption is true.
cards.explanation: Systems Manager decrypts a SecureString value for a GetParameter request with WithDecryption enabled, subject to the caller's permissions.

cards.statement: AWS Systems Manager keeps an advanced parameter's Expiration timestamp when the parameter value changes.
cards.explanation: A value update preserves the Expiration policy's timestamp. Change or remove the policy to adjust when Systems Manager deletes the parameter.

source.title: Assigning parameter policies in Parameter Store

cards.statement: AWS CodeBuild resolves env/secrets-manager references into environment values for build commands.
cards.explanation: A buildspec can name a Secrets Manager secret under env/secrets-manager. CodeBuild retrieves its value under the chosen environment variable name.

cards.statement: AWS CodeBuild supports masking a secret after build code base64-encodes the retrieved env/secrets-manager value.
cards.explanation: CodeBuild masks the exact secret value it retrieves. A transformed value, such as a base64-encoded copy, can appear in logs, so build code handles sanitization.
cards.misconception: CodeBuild recognizes and masks encoded derivatives of a retrieved secret.

cards.statement: DynamoDB can return a permitted subset for a request that asks for attributes denied by dynamodb:Attributes.
cards.explanation: dynamodb:Attributes restricts the attributes a caller requests. A request outside that permission is denied; IAM does not redact it into an allowed subset.
cards.misconception: DynamoDB removes forbidden attributes from a response instead of denying the request.

source.title: Using IAM policy conditions for fine-grained access control

cards.statement: Amazon S3 supports tenant-specific object prefixes in IAM policies that use ${aws:PrincipalTag/tenant}.
cards.explanation: IAM substitutes the caller's tenant tag into the S3 object resource ARN. An allowed ARN ending in that tenant's prefix restricts the covered object operations.

source.title: IAM policy elements: Variables and tags

cards.statement: A Python Lambda .zip package for handler app.handler places app.py at the archive root.
cards.explanation: For a handler configured as app.handler, Lambda imports app.py as a top-level module. Put that file at the root of the deployment archive.

source.title: Working with .zip file archives for Python Lambda functions

cards.statement: AWS Lambda extracts a layer's archive into /opt in the function's execution environment.
cards.explanation: Layer contents land under /opt. Package dependencies in the directory layout expected by the function's runtime so it can find them.

cards.statement: Lambda supplies a runtime interface client to functions built from a Debian base image.
cards.explanation: For a Lambda image built from a Debian base image, include a runtime interface client during the image build. That client communicates with the Lambda Runtime API.
cards.misconception: Lambda injects a runtime interface client into a function's custom base image during invocation.

source.title: Create a Lambda function using a container image

cards.statement: Lambda gives container functions a writable root filesystem for generated application files.
cards.explanation: Lambda runs container images with a read-only root filesystem. Code writes temporary files to /tmp instead.
cards.misconception: A Lambda container image has the writable root filesystem typical of a local container.

source.title: Create a Lambda function using a container image

cards.statement: Amazon ECR returns ImageTagAlreadyExistsException when a push targets an existing immutable tag.
cards.explanation: A push using a tag protected by tag immutability fails rather than overwriting the referenced image. Choose a new tag for the next image.

source.title: Preventing image tags from being overwritten in Amazon ECR

cards.statement: An AWS CodeArtifact authorization token can access repositories across its issuing domain.
cards.explanation: CodeArtifact tokens are scoped to a domain, so a token can authenticate to its repositories subject to the caller's repository permissions.

cards.statement: AWS CodeBuild selects build runtimes from runtime-versions in the build phase of a buildspec.
cards.explanation: CodeBuild reads runtime-versions from the buildspec's install phase. It selects runtimes available in the chosen build image.
cards.misconception: The runtime-versions mapping belongs under the build phase instead of the install phase.

cards.statement: AWS CodeBuild includes the paths under cache/paths in the build's output artifact.
cards.explanation: cache/paths identifies files to cache for future builds. The buildspec's artifacts section selects the build output files.
cards.misconception: The cache file list also determines the build's output artifact contents.

cards.statement: AWS CodeBuild can use StartBuild's computeTypeOverride to change the project's saved compute configuration.
cards.explanation: computeTypeOverride selects compute resources for the build being started. It overrides the project's setting for that build, rather than updating the saved project.
cards.misconception: A compute type override on StartBuild changes the compute setting saved in the project.

cards.statement: Elastic Beanstalk reads .ebextensions configuration files written in YAML or JSON.
cards.explanation: Put files with a .config extension under .ebextensions in the application bundle. Elastic Beanstalk parses them to configure the environment.

source.title: Advanced environment customization with configuration files (.ebextensions)

cards.statement: AWS AppConfig supports a JSON Schema validator for checking free form configuration before deployment.
cards.explanation: AppConfig checks free form configuration against the schema you supply. A schema validation failure blocks deploying that configuration.

cards.statement: A Lambda validator's normal return of an error message signals validation failure to AWS AppConfig.
cards.explanation: A Lambda validator signals AppConfig validation failure by throwing an exception. A successful return containing an error message does not signal that failure.
cards.misconception: AppConfig treats an error message in a successful Lambda return value as validation failure.

cards.statement: AWS SAM's sam local start-api runs local HTTP endpoints for Lambda functions with API events.
cards.explanation: SAM starts a local server that routes HTTP requests to your configured Lambda handlers, letting you exercise API payloads during development.

source.title: Introduction to testing with sam local start-api

cards.statement: AWS SAM sam local invoke redirects the function's AWS SDK calls to built-in service emulators.
cards.explanation: SAM runs the Lambda function locally. Its SDK calls target their configured endpoints, so tests can reach live AWS resources unless you supply mocks or emulators.
cards.misconception: SAM's local invocation emulates the AWS services that function code calls through an SDK.

source.title: How to test serverless functions and applications

cards.statement: AWS SAM uses deployment parameter overrides to vary the same template's settings between environments.
cards.explanation: Define parameters in the SAM template and supply deployment-specific overrides. Those values take precedence over parameter defaults in the template.

cards.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API TestInvokeMethod needs a deployed stage to test a configured method.
cards.explanation: TestInvokeMethod simulates a configured REST API method before API deployment. It lets the developer test the method through the API Gateway management interface.
cards.misconception: TestInvokeMethod requires an existing REST API stage deployment.

source.title: Invoke REST APIs in API Gateway

cards.statement: A REST API mock integration in Amazon API Gateway returns data produced by its response mapping template.
cards.explanation: For a REST API mock integration, an integration response mapping template generates a response body for the caller, allowing a developer to simulate backend output.

source.title: Mock integrations for REST APIs in API Gateway

cards.statement: Amazon API Gateway REST API stages use the latest saved integration settings for incoming requests.
cards.explanation: A stage serves its associated deployment. REST API integration changes take effect there after a new deployment is associated with the stage.
cards.misconception: Saving an integration change updates the behavior of an existing REST API stage.

source.title: Create a deployment for a REST API in API Gateway

cards.statement: Amazon EventBridge TestEventPattern returns a boolean in the Result field for the supplied event.
cards.explanation: TestEventPattern compares the supplied event with the supplied pattern. Result tells the caller whether that event matches the pattern.

cards.statement: AWS Step Functions TestState supports inspectionData.request at DEBUG level for an HTTP Task.
cards.explanation: TestState uses TRACE for HTTP request details in inspectionData.request. DEBUG shows intermediate state input and output processing results.
cards.misconception: DEBUG inspection includes the HTTP request field provided by TRACE.

cards.statement: AWS Lambda Invoke with InvocationType=DryRun checks the caller's lambda:InvokeFunction permission.
cards.explanation: DryRun validates the request parameters and the caller's permission to invoke the function. It provides a permission check while leaving the handler unexecuted.

cards.statement: A Lambda test event for an API Gateway HTTP API places binary request bytes in body as a base64 string.
cards.explanation: An HTTP API Lambda proxy event carries binary request data as a base64-encoded body with isBase64Encoded set to true. Handler code decodes body to recover the bytes.

source.title: Handling binary data using Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs

cards.statement: AWS CodeBuild builds test reports from test runner output printed to the build's standard output.
cards.explanation: CodeBuild reads test result files selected by reports/files in the buildspec. Configure the test runner to write a supported report format.
cards.misconception: CodeBuild parses a test runner's console output to populate its test reports.

cards.statement: AWS AppSync EvaluateMappingTemplate sends the evaluated request to the resolver's configured data source.
cards.explanation: EvaluateMappingTemplate evaluates the supplied template and context in isolation. It returns evaluationResult rather than executing the resolver's data source request.
cards.misconception: EvaluateMappingTemplate executes the data source operation produced by a request mapping template.
